title: How a Nature Cruise Turned Into a Nightmare
partialText: The hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius set off alarms for a world still traumatized by Covid. For those on board, the danger was much closer.

title: Trump Uses Taiwan Arms Sales as Bargaining Chip With China, in a Risky Move
partialText: The president said a potential arms deal for Taiwan was a “very good negotiating chip” in talks with Beijing. His words raise questions about the reliability of U.S. support.

title: Rubio, Once a China Hawk, Strikes Softer Tone to Align With Trump
partialText: As a senator, Marco Rubio even hinted at the need for regime change in China. Now he talks about cooperation.

title: China Will Host Putin, Days After Trump’s Visit
partialText: The Russian leader will go to Beijing on Tuesday for talks with President Xi Jinping. The Kremlin said he had watched President Trump’s visit closely.

title: In Congress, a Sexual Harassment ‘Minefield’ Persists, Aides and Former Staff Say
partialText: Nearly 10 years after Congress instituted measures to make it easier for women to lodge harassment complaints, lawmakers and aides say the behavior is still rampant.

title: A Bitter Land Commissioner Race in New Mexico Over 9 Million Acres
partialText: A Republican candidate for the state land commissioner post has Democrats worried that protected state and federal land could be opened to industry.

title: What to Watch in Saturday’s Republican Senate Primary in Louisiana
partialText: Senator Bill Cassidy, who has drawn President Trump’s ire, is fighting for political survival.

title: Political Money Is Flowing to Influencers. But From Whom?
partialText: Social media stars have become a magnet for campaigns and political groups that want to push priorities without disclosing where their money is going.

title: Which Countries Are Profiting From the Iran War Oil Shock
partialText: An analysis of oil export data offers clues about which nations have benefited from higher prices, and which have lost a lot of revenue.

title: Hamas’s Top Leader in Gaza Is Killed in Israeli Strike
partialText: Izz al-Din al-Haddad took over the group’s military wing in Gaza last year. Hamas officials confirmed Mr. al-Haddad’s death in an Israeli attack.

title: Trump Says a Top ISIS Leader Was Killed in a U.S.-Nigerian Mission
partialText: Abu Bilal al-Minuki, said to be the Islamic State’s second-ranking leader, was killed after a helicopter-borne assault by commandos from both countries on Friday night, two U.S. officials said.

title: They Fled to Safety in Palestinian Territory, Then Settlers Attacked Again
partialText: Violent settlers are not merely clearing Palestinians from land under Israel’s control. They are attacking areas where Israel agreed to Palestinian self-governance.

title: LIRR Labor Strike Shuts Down Busiest U.S. Passenger Rail Service
partialText: This is the first strike on the service in more than 30 years. It comes after three years of failed contract negotiations, two federal interventions and a volley of last-minute bargaining.

title: Long Island Rail Road Workers Are on Strike. Here’s What to Know.
partialText: America’s busiest passenger rail service shut down on Saturday after unions and transit officials failed to agree on a new contract.

title: What A.I. Kant Do
partialText: Could we English majors have a future after all?

title: Stephen Colbert’s Late Show Cancellation and the Fall of CBS
partialText: In shutting down a 33-year late-night franchise, CBS is assenting to its own diminishment.

title: Finishing School
partialText: It’s graduation season, a time of aspiration and anxiety. Today is about the aspiration — the wisdom to be gleaned from great commencement addresses.

title: Jack Douglas, Producer for Aerosmith and Lennon, Dies at 80
partialText: A onetime Beatlemaniac, he helped shape the sound of hits like “Walk This Way” and “(Just Like) Starting Over.”

title: Man Stole Medieval Skull From Church and Sealed it in Concrete, Police Say
partialText: The man disagreed with the 800-year-old relic’s display in a church in the Czech Republic and planned to throw it into a river, police said.

title: Navy Aircraft Carrier to Complete Longest Deployment Since Vietnam
partialText: After being diverted for combat with Venezuela and Iran, the U.S.S. Gerald R. Ford will return to Norfolk, Va., on Saturday after nearly a year at sea.
